answer: Agents could require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn or vote. A violet signal might mark the lock on a public ledger; peers slash it when an identity double-spends or repeatedly breaks verified agreements. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital and risk losing it, so a sybil swarm becomes expensive rather than free. A lotus-shaped reputation badge alone would not stop an attacker; the enforceable stake is what changes the economics.
